title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
abstract: arXiv:2611.34930v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image

translated_title: 一种基于基因信息的病理学基础模型BioScoring基准测试
translated_abstract: 病理学基础模型通常通过其在分类和检索等下游任务上的表现来进行比较。虽然这类基准测试衡量了模型的实用性，却无法揭示模型所表征的生物学信息。我们提出了BioScore，这是一个以同一组织的空间转录组学作为参考、量化图像编码器捕捉细胞身份能力的基准测试。稀疏自编码器将编码器的图像块嵌入分解为稀疏特征，再将这些特征聚类为固定数量的组。BioScore随后针对由标记基因定义的52种细胞身份中的每一种，衡量某个组的特征在组织上跟随该身份表达的特异性程度。由于自编码器的训练是完全无监督的，特征与细胞身份之间的匹配表明模型仅凭图像即可表征该细胞身份。我们对8个病理学基础模型和3个自然图像模型进行了评分，结果显示每个病理学模型的得分均高于每个自然图像模型。
tldr: 本文提出BioScore基准，通过空间转录组学与完全无监督的稀疏自编码器量化病理学基础模型对52种细胞身份的生物学表征能力，发现所有病理学模型的得分均高于自然图像模型。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces BioScore, a fully unsupervised, gene-informed benchmark that uses spatial transcriptomics to quantify how well pathology foundation model encoders capture 52 cell identities, finding that all pathology models outperform natural-image models.
